summary: Democratic senator from California since December 2024 after 24 years in the House, where he chaired the Intelligence Committee and was lead manager in Donald Trump's first impeachment trial in 2020. The Republican House censured him in 2023 over the Trump-Russia investigation; he won the Senate seat in 2024 after spending heavily to lift a Republican, Steve Garvey, into the top-two runoff. Since May 2025 he has been the subject of a Trump-administration mortgage-fraud referral that Maryland prosecutors had not found grounds to charge as of late 2025.

works.title: Midnight in Washington

chapters.title: Prosecutor and state senator
chapters.dek: A Soviet-spy case and two lost races before a seat in Sacramento.
chapters.body:
Schiff was born in Framingham, Massachusetts, on June 22, 1960, and grew up in Arizona and then Alamo, California [[wikipedia, schiff-senate-bio]]. His family belonged to Temple Sinai, a Reform congregation in Glendale; he describes his family's story as "from the shtetl to the Congress in three generations" [[jta-2024]]. He studied political science at Stanford and graduated from Harvard Law School in 1985 [[wikipedia]].

As an assistant U.S. attorney in Los Angeles from 1987 to 1993 he prosecuted Richard Miller, the first FBI agent indicted for spying for the Soviet Union; it took three trials to secure a conviction that stood [[wikipedia, schiff-senate-bio]]. He lost a 1994 special election and rematch for the State Assembly to James Rogan, then won a State Senate seat in 1996, where he chaired the Judiciary Committee [[wikipedia, schiff-senate-bio]].

chapters.title: Twenty-four years in the House
chapters.dek: Beating an impeachment manager, then rising on the Intelligence Committee.
chapters.body:
In 2000 Schiff defeated Rogan, by then one of the House managers in Bill Clinton's impeachment, in what was the most expensive House race to that point [[wikipedia]]. He was reelected eleven times as his Los Angeles-area district became more Democratic, and served on the Judiciary, Foreign Affairs and Appropriations committees [[wikipedia, schiff-senate-bio]]. In 2015 he said he regretted his vote for the 2003 invasion of Iraq [[wikipedia]].

He joined the Intelligence Committee in 2008 and became its senior Democrat in 2015, which put him at the center of Congress's response to Russian interference in the 2016 election [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Trump's chief antagonist in Congress
chapters.dek: Russia, Ukraine, impeachment, January 6 and censure.
chapters.body:
As ranking member and, from January 2019, chairman of the Intelligence Committee, Schiff led Democrats' Trump-Russia inquiry and then the Ukraine investigation that produced Trump's impeachment on December 18, 2019 [[wikipedia]]. As lead House manager in the Senate trial, he closed his January 23, 2020, argument to a silent chamber: "Because right matters. And the truth matters. Otherwise, we are lost" [[usatoday-closing-2020]]. The Senate acquitted Trump in February [[wikipedia]]. He later sat on the January 6 committee and led its fourth public hearing, and published Midnight in Washington in 2021 [[wikipedia]].

After Republicans won the House, they censured him on June 21, 2023, by 213 to 209, over his statements on Trump and Russia; the sponsor dropped a proposed $16 million fine to win the votes. Schiff called the censure a "badge of honor" and said, "I will not yield" [[ap-censure-2023]]. Trump has called him "the enemy within" and demanded he face trial [[jta-2024]].

chapters.title: The Senate race
chapters.dek: A top-two strategy that lifted a Republican, and a call for Biden to step aside.
chapters.body:
Schiff announced for Dianne Feinstein's seat on January 26, 2023, and Nancy Pelosi endorsed him days later [[wikipedia]]. California's top-two primary shaped his strategy. His campaign spent about $38 million before the March 2024 primary, much of it on ads, including on Fox News and in mail to Republicans, that called Steve Garvey "too conservative for California" and raised Garvey's profile among Republican voters. Schiff finished with 31.6 percent to Garvey's 31.5, shutting out Katie Porter, who called the tactic "the Schiff gift to the Republican Party in California" [[calmatters-primary-2024]].

On July 17, 2024, he became the most prominent Democrat to that point to ask Joe Biden to "pass the torch," saying he had "serious concerns about whether the President can defeat Donald Trump" [[npr-biden-2024]]. Biden withdrew four days later [[wikipedia]]. Schiff beat Garvey in November and was sworn in on December 9, 2024 [[toi-win-2024, wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Senator under investigation
chapters.dek: A mortgage-fraud referral from a Trump appointee, and a stalled grand jury.
chapters.body:
Shortly after taking office Schiff told JTA that the country was "very much weakened as a democracy" and that antisemitism had grown on both left and right since October 7, 2023 [[jta-2024]]. In May 2025 Bill Pulte, Trump's director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, sent the Justice Department a criminal referral alleging Schiff had falsified bank documents and property records to get better loan terms. Attorney General Pam Bondi appointed Ed Martin as a special attorney on the case, and a grand jury in Maryland took it up [[nbc-referral-2025, tnnd-referral-2025]]. Schiff called it "the kind of stuff you see tinpot dictators do"; his lawyer, Preet Bharara, called the allegations "transparently false, stale, and long debunked" [[nbc-referral-2025]].

In October 2025 NBC reported, citing four people familiar with the case, that Maryland prosecutors had not found enough evidence to charge him and that the inquiry "came to a standstill," though no final decision had been made and the U.S. attorney was told to pursue more evidence [[nbc-stalled-2025]]. A year later Schiff was campaigning for his party's midterm candidates, predicting on Meet the Press that Democrats would win both chambers if they could hold off "dark money" spending [[nbc-mtp-2026]].
